sources.title: VTOL Urban Air Mobility Concept Vehicles for Technology Development
sources.authors: Silva, C.; Johnson, W.; Solis, E.; Patterson, M. D.; Antcliff, K. R.
sources.venue: AIAA Aviation Technology, Integration, and Operations Conference, AIAA 2018-3847, doi:10.2514/6.2018-3847
sources.summary: Defines the NASA RVLT UAM reference vehicles (quadrotor, side-by-side, lift+cruise) sized in NDARC to a common 6-passenger (1,200 lb payload) mission. The lift+cruise has 8 RPM-controlled fixed-pitch lift rotors on booms, a high wing and one pusher; the paper gives a complete weight/power/drag breakdown and the battery, motor and accessory technology factors.
sources.project_use: WP M/D: closest published reference for our configuration; use Table 3 as a scaling and sanity check of weight fractions, disk loading, D/q, L/De and hover C-rate; use the battery derating chain (cell -> usable -> installed) and motor accessory factor in the sizing code. WP V: benchmark for the sizing model.
sources.credibility: High. NASA RVLT authors; NDARC-based conceptual design, not flight data. Technology level is 'advanced' (650 Wh/kg cell), so battery numbers must be re-based to today's cells.
key_data: Battery: cell 650 Wh/kg -> minus 20% (5% top + 15% bottom of charge) = 530 Wh/kg usable -> 30% weight for BMS/pack structure -> 400 Wh/kg installed (p.10, Sec. VI.A)
Motor weight W = 0.3928 Q^0.8587 (NDARC empirical relation; units as defined in the NDARC manual, SZ05), accessory (inverter, cooling, wiring) factor 1.63 x motor weight (p.11, Eq. 1)
Electric lift+cruise (Table 3): DGW 8,210 lb, empty 7,001 lb, payload 1,200 lb, 8 lifters, radius 5.0 ft, disk loading 13.1 lb/ft2, hover tip speed 585 ft/s, thrust-weighted solidity 0.267
Electric lift+cruise (Table 3): battery 1,436 MJ, 1,693 lb; MRP 139 hp per lifter; pusher 628 hp; D/q 16.9 ft2; L/De 8.5; aircraft hover FM 0.74; hover C-rate 2.4 /hr; cruise C-rate 0.7 /hr
Lift rotor diameter capped at 10 ft for RPM-control responsiveness (p.11); hover tip speed kept ~550-600 ft/s for noise (p.14)
Hover C-rate relation x_hover ~ sqrt(W/2rhoA) * eta_cruise (L/De) / (eta_hover FM Range) (Eq. 3, p.11)
Lift+cruise FM highest of the three types 'due to the very small download' (p.14)

sources.authors: Johnson, W.; Silva, C.; Solis, E.
sources.venue: AHS Technical Conference on Aeromechanics Design for Transformative Vertical Flight, San Francisco, Jan. 2018
sources.summary: The original NASA air-taxi concept set, including a single-passenger (250 lb payload, 50 nm) electric quadrotor that is the closest NASA reference to our payload class. Gives the battery technology table used across NASA UAM work and weight-vs-range sensitivity.
sources.project_use: WP M/D: battery technology levels and installation fractions; the 1-passenger electric quadrotor (DGW ~1,250 lb) is a direct mass-scale benchmark for a 200 kg payload aircraft and for the range sensitivity check (50/100/150 km).
sources.credibility: High (NASA). Conceptual design results; the 1-pax vehicle is a multicopter, not lift+cruise.
key_data: Table 2 battery technology: uninstalled 240/300/325/487.5/650 Wh/kg; usable fraction 70/75/80/80/80%; installation fraction 0.8/0.5/0.3/0.3/0.3; installed 93/150/200/300/400 Wh/kg; max burst discharge 4/6/8/14/20 C; DoD max 0.80-0.85
Discharge currents must be limited to 2-3C for good battery life (p.4)
1-pax electric quadrotor (Table 9): DGW 1,252 lb, WE 997 lb, battery 272 lb / 178 MJ, disk loading 2.5 lb/ft2, radius 6.31 ft, 4 x 21.6 hp, tip speed 450 ft/s, D/q 3.43 ft2, Vbr 86 kt
Doubling range to 100 nm increases DGW of the 1-pax electric quadrotor by 50%; no closure at 200 nm (p.8)

sources.title: AC 21.17-4, Type Certification - Powered-lift

PL.2230: limit loads = structural design loads; ultimate = limit x 1.5 unless otherwise provided (Appendix A)
PL.2270: emergency landing must include dynamic conditions; occupant loads within human-injury criteria; items of mass near cabin restrained (Appendix A)
PL.2430(a)(1): energy system independence so that failure of one component does not cause unacceptable loss of energy supply; (b)(2) energy storage isolated from occupant compartments

sources.title: 14 CFR 23.337 Limit maneuvering load factors (pre-Amendment 23-64 text, 1-1-16 edition)
sources.summary: The prescriptive normal-category manoeuvre load factor formula that ASTM F3116 and our requirements (n = +3.8/-1.5) descend from; also contains the 23.341 gust load factor formula.
sources.project_use: WP F/M: limit load factors and gust load factor formula (Pratt) for the V-n diagram.
sources.credibility: High (law, historical edition). Superseded by performance-based Part 23 amdt 64 + ASTM F3116; numbers still the accepted means.
key_data: Normal category positive limit n >= 2.1 + 24,000/(W + 10,000), W in lb, need not exceed 3.8 (23.337(a)(1))
Negative limit n >= 0.4 x positive for normal category (23.337(b)(1))
Gust: n = 1 + Kg Ude V a / (498 W/S), Kg = 0.88 mu_g/(5.3 + mu_g), mu_g = 2(W/S)/(rho C a g) (23.341(c))

HIC <= 1,000; shoulder strap <= 1,750 lb (single) / 2,000 lb (dual); pelvis-lumbar compressive load <= 1,500 lb; 170 lb ATD (49 CFR 572 subpart B)
